challenge.better_approach: Considered only adding the retry: measured that the commons pull is a no-op under artifact quiet (the bare pull fetched 11 commits the quiet pull had not), so a retry alone would fail all 3 tries. Considered changing _quiet to chdir into -C: that is the artifact tool's interface, used by others, and outside cc; calling it correctly from cc's own script is the smaller change and stays inside one component (RULE 1).
challenge.hidden_assumption: That a rejected push names 'fetch first' or 'non-fast-forward' in its stderr (measured: git 2.x prints '! [rejected] main -> main (fetch first)'); the retry keys on the push failing with the pull before it succeeding, not on the English text, so a localized git still retries; a push that fails for a reason a pull cannot cure (auth, no network) costs 3 tries and then stops loud exactly as today.
challenge.prior_art: 979a63671481 (PROVED) made close.sh stop loud with exit 5 on an unpushed repo; its proof's diverged-commons tooth passes on rc 0 OR on any NOT PUSHED naming the commons, so it reads green over this bug. Memory artifact-quiet-runs-in-cairn-root (2026-11-13) recorded the cwd fact for hand pulls; no ticket carries it. Grepped tickets and questions for 'artifact quiet' and '_quiet': 8 hits, all PROVED, none about the cwd.
challenge.real_collision: 979a63671481's clause that an unpushed close stops before any crossing stands: after the 3rd rejected push this still stops with exit 5. Distinction, not collision. RULE 1: close.sh is cc's script and calls the artifact tool's published quiet verb.

answers.falsifier: Over scratch origins: a close whose commons origin moved before it exits 0 with the commons 0 ahead and both commits on origin; one whose origin moves once between its pull and its push does the same; one whose origin moves before every push stops with exit 5 and NOT PUSHED naming the commons after exactly 3 pushes; an in-sync close is unchanged. Horizon: the rest of today's host-tool batch closes without an exit 5. Wrong intent if close should never push the commons (then the step belongs to another door).
answers.from_idea: none, because it was measured, not imagined: /home/akien/.akien/temp/close_ddbaaf055105_105122.log on akiendelllinux is the bash -x trace of the failing close, 2026-11-23
answers.how: In cairn/devices/cc/scripts/close.sh sync_repo, run every git through `git -C "$d"` and hold `cairn artifact quiet -C "$d"`; when the push is rejected because origin moved ('fetch first' / non-fast-forward), pull --rebase and push again, at most 3 pushes in all, then NOT PUSHED as now. A red-first proof beside close.sh drives close.sh as written over scratch bare origins, with a git shim on PATH that pushes another hand's commit to the commons origin before close's push.
answers.traces_to: Law 7 (errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces and permanent in records of truth: today the close's NOT PUSHED is loud but names the wrong cause, and the records it means to land are left unpushed) and Law 3 (measured: the pull that close.sh believes updates the commons updates the house).
answers.what: A close's sync of the commons pulls and pushes the commons itself, under the commons' own door lock, and retries a push that origin outran, so a close does not exit 5 merely because another hand pushed to the commons.

bullets.text: close.sh's sync_repo has never pulled the commons: `cairn artifact quiet -- git pull` runs git from the cairn root (bin/cairn chdirs there, _quiet passes no cwd), so the 'commons' pull re-pulls the house under the house's lock, and the commons push fails whenever origin moved at all. 979a's proof accepts that NOT PUSHED as a pass.
Today's three close exit 5s (a577 once, ddba twice) were this, made frequent by another hand crossing tickets into the commons every few seconds.

title: A close's sync of the commons pulls and pushes the commons itself, under the commons' own door lock, and retries a push
